title: Shallow ComCat centers had more excess M5.5 and M5.8 neighbors than intermediate centers in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested nearby earthquake counts around 866 ComCat centers of preferred magnitude 6.5 to below 7.5 in 2001-2024. We subtracted days 1-30 before each center from days 1-30 after it, used a 200 km distance through the Earth, and held the center magnitude distribution fixed. The shallow-minus-intermediate excess was 0.683 neighbors per center at magnitude 5.5 or more, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 0.262 to 1.154. At magnitude 5.8 or more, it was 0.343 (0.071 to 0.634). The added 5.5 to below 5.8 band contributed 0.340 (0.164 to 0.541). The excess stayed positive after isolation on both sides of each center. Days 7-30 and the 2013-2024 subset had uncertain contrasts. This extends an earlier GCMT test. Catalogs and events overlap, so this is not independent confirmation. Mixed magnitude types, location error, regional differences, selected windows and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The count difference does not identify causal aftershocks or a physical mechanism.

display.caption: Magnitude-standardized shallow-minus-intermediate excess counts. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. The main window is 1 inclusive to 30 exclusive days on each side. Days 7-30 and recent-year checks include zero.

citations.reason: Prior count protocol and threshold sensitivity set this test. Catalog events and source estimates overlap.
